title: Cadre runner capability manifest (roster/runner-capabilities.json)
description: Declarative, build-time source of truth for the data idea #8 (REQ-CADRE-BACKLOG-8) found hardcoded across generate_global_plugin.py's CAPABILITY_PROFILES/ALLOWED_MODELS/ALLOWED_CODEX_MODELS/ALLOWED_REASONING_EFFORTS, generate_role_metadata.py's TIER_MAP, and the structural runner-divergence facts from .agents/skills/run-agent-orchestration/references/runner-adapters.md (CM-FR-1..8, plus native_workspace_isolation and the prompt_hook_*/tool_gate_* pair added later). Read at build time by roster/orchestration/src/generate_global_plugin.py and generate_role_metadata.py, which load capability_tiers/model_tiers/allowed_reasoning_efforts directly with stdlib json so those Python constants can never drift from this file, and ALSO at dispatch time by roster/orchestration/mcp/dispatch_core.py (model_tiers) and mcp/api_runner.py (capability_tiers, deciding fail-closed which tools an api-runner dispatch offers). OD-2 is therefore narrower than 'this file has no runtime consumer', and the narrow form is the part that matters: the runner-divergence facts -- native_workspace_isolation and the prompt_hook_*/tool_gate_* pair -- are descriptive build-time data that no dispatch-time code path may branch on, because tool_gate_support names an enforcement boundary and code that skipped a check because a data file said 'none' would be a security control decided by JSON (see requirements.md OD-2 disposition; roster/orchestration/test/test_runner_capabilities.py enforces it across every module under roster/orchestration/). This schema validates the manifest's own shape/type/enum content in isolation, matching roster/catalog.schema.json's precedent (Draft 2020-12, validated by a jsonschema-guarded standalone check, never a required runtime dependency of the generators themselves).

native_workspace_isolation.description: Which runner-native mechanism, if any, isolates a dispatched role's edits into a separate workspace before it runs (see roster/shared/workspace-isolation.md, which every write-capable role follows regardless of this value). Build-time descriptive data only -- no dispatch-time code currently reads this field (matching this manifest's own OD-2 disposition for its other fields).

prompt_hook_support.description: Whether the runner can run something on every user prompt BEFORE the model sees it, and whether that thing can put text into the model's context. "context_injection": the hook's output reaches the model. "dispatch_only": a hook fires but its output is discarded, so it can observe and act out-of-band but cannot steer the turn -- distinguished from "none" because the two look identical from inside a hook script, which runs and exits 0 either way. "none": no per-prompt hook surface at all. Descriptive only; nothing branches on it at dispatch time.

prompt_hook_mechanism.description: The concrete per-prompt surface named in runner-adapters.md, or null when prompt_hook_support is "none". For "dispatch_only" this must say what is discarded, not just what exists.

tool_gate_support.description: Whether a hook can refuse a tool call in the user's OWN session (not merely in a subagent session the suite itself starts). "blocking": the runner awaits the hook and honors a refusal. "advisory": a hook observes the call but cannot stop it. "none": no pre-tool hook surface. This is the field that decides whether an orchestration policy is enforceable on a runner or is only a strong suggestion.

tool_gate_mechanism.description: The concrete pre-tool surface and the shape of a refusal, or null when tool_gate_support is "none".
